bug_semantics: UnsafeBlitFormatterBase.Deserialize (Unity blit resolvers) reads an attacker-controlled inner byteLength from a MessagePack extension body and allocates new T[byteLength / elementSize] before checking that value against the already-bounded extension header length or remaining payload bytes. A tiny ext payload can declare an enormous byteLength, forcing a huge T[] allocation (CWE-770) on UnityBlitResolver / UnityBlitWithPrimitiveArrayResolver paths used for vectors, matrices, and primitive arrays. CVE-2026-48514 / GHSA-w567-gjr2-hm5j is PUBLISHED (not withdrawn/rejected) and is fixed by rejecting negative, unaligned, or mismatched byteLength before allocation.
flaw_origin: The unbounded blit allocation was first written on 2017-02-24 in d8a42395ae66122772057a4125155b02670bf7a3 (neuecc, 'testing extremly fast ext vector[] copy for Unity'), which added src/MessagePack.UnityShims/Extension/Vector3ArrayFormatter.cs with UnsafeBlitFormatterBase.Deserialize doing var byteLength = MessagePackBinary.ReadInt32(...) then var result = new T[byteLength / StructLength] with no remaining-length check. Immediate parent 5bb2909d9e0e59cb129d2ee2d8d256af5d2f8c88 has no blit formatter. Later commits only moved/renamed the file, ported the same Deserialize onto MessagePackReader, and expanded formatter subclasses; they did not first introduce the mechanism.
